question: The EU has been and remains the largest donor to the Ukrainian state since Russia first invaded Ukraine: EUR 168.9 billion1 has been mobilised in support of Ukraine; of this total, EUR 15 billion2 has been mobilised on the basis of bilateral agreements with the Member States.

In order to provide correct and transparent information to taxpaying EU citizens, it is vital that they be properly informed on every aspect of this financial aid. In view of the recent statement by the Ukrainian Minister of Defence that Romania would be granting its 23rd package of military aid to the administration in Kyiv3, can the Commission state: 1.
What Romania’s contribution has been to the total aid granted to Ukraine so far?
What the aid packages granted by Romania since the start of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine have consisted of, and what future aid has been pledged by Romania?
To what extent the support provided through green corridors, including the Black Sea corridors, has been factored into the calculation of the reinforced financial aid granted by Romania?
answer: Since the beginning of Russia’s war of aggression, the EU and Member States have mobilised EUR 187.3 billion in support to Ukraine and its citizens as of 3 December 2025. This amount includes EUR 15 billion in bilateral financial and humanitarian assistance from the Member States.

The Commission does not have access to the details of the bilateral financial assistance packages that Member States provide to Ukraine and communicate to the Commission. The above-mentioned total amount also includes approximately EUR 17 billion of support mobilised by the EU and its Member States to support people fleeing Ukraine.

However, support enabling the transport of goods to and from Ukraine via Member States’ territories is not included in the above quantification. This exclusion is due to the complexity of this type of support as it also generates revenues through increased traffic on EU rail, road and ports infrastructure and increased fees to be paid to national authorities.
